blocks.heading: What the Labels Mean for Your Plan
rows: Deaf
The Act's specified-disability list defines deaf as 70 dB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears.
Many deaf students use Indian Sign Language (ISL) as their first language and read and write the school language as a second one.
A sign language interpreter, captions, written notes and a seat with a clear view of the speaker.
Hard of hearing
Defined as 60 dB to 70 dB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears.
Many use hearing aids and spoken language, and tire quickly in noise, group talk and phone calls.
A quiet seat, captions, slides and notes in advance, and meetings run one speaker at a time.
Deafened later in life, or one-sided loss
Loss that does not meet the two definitions above may not count as a benchmark disability, so check the assessment.
Needs vary a lot. Some people sign, some lip-read, some rely on devices.
Ask the medical board what your result means before you plan around a quota.

blocks.heading: School and Exam Help
rows: CBSE school boards

The CBSE consolidated circular of 18 February 2016 lets candidates with hearing impairment study one compulsory language instead of two in Class X, and names speech or hearing defects for third-language exemption in Classes VI to VIII. It also allows a scribe, extra time or both: for a three-hour paper the extra time is 60 minutes, for two hours it is 40 minutes.

The circular does not say outright whether deaf students are covered by the scribe and extra-time rule, so ask the CBSE regional office or helpline 1800-11-8002. Requests go through the school head with a medical certificate, ideally in Class IX or XI.
Entrance exams and government recruitment

The wider rules in our guide to careers for students with disabilities apply: DEPwD's memorandum of 10 August 2022 sets compensatory time of at least 20 minutes per hour, and JEE Main and CLAT give benchmark-disability candidates extra time.
A deaf candidate usually needs extra time for reading speed in the second language more than a scribe. Ask for what you need in the form, not at the centre.
Listening and oral components
Language papers with listening or speaking parts need a written rule from the board. We found no general exemption order, so each board and exam has to say what it allows.
Ask the exam body early which alternative it gives, such as a reader passage or written task.

blocks.heading: Access: What to Ask For, and Why
rows: Lectures and classes
A sign language interpreter or live captioning, slides and notes before class, and permission to record where allowed.
Following a class is the first barrier. Without access, marks measure the missing access, not the student.
Group work and discussion
One speaker at a time, a shared chat or written summary, and a note-taker.
Fast overlapping talk is the hardest setting for both deaf and hard-of-hearing students.
Exams
Extra time, written instructions and an alternative to any listening component.
Second-language reading speed, not knowledge, often limits deaf students under time pressure.
Internships and first jobs
Written task briefs, captions on calls, chat for quick questions and a named person to go to.
Most early jobs run on spoken instruction. Asking for written instructions is a normal request.

blocks.heading: Courses Built for Deaf Students
rows: Diploma in Teaching Indian Sign Language (DTISL)
2 years
For deaf candidates. ISLRTC says only deaf candidates can study it, and the AYJNISHD notice asks for 10+2 with 45 percent and a Certificate of Disability (Deaf).
Teaching ISL to interpreters, officials and students. RCI approved the programme in 2018.
Diploma in Indian Sign Language Interpretation (DISLI)
2 years
For hearing candidates. Entry needs 10+2 with 50 percent, functional hands, fluency in a language and hearing in the normal range.
Interpreting. Deaf students should not pay for it expecting to become interpreters.
B.Ed. Special Education (Hearing Impairment)
2 years
Bachelor's degree in any subject with 50 percent (AYJNISHD 2025-26 notice, with extra background rules at some centres).
Teaching in schools for deaf and hard-of-hearing children, which usually needs RCI registration.
D.Ed. Special Education (Hearing Impairment)
2 years
10+2 with 50 percent (45 percent for SC, ST and PwD candidates).
Special-school teaching roles at the level RCI allows. Confirm the current RCI rules for your state.
B.ASLP (audiology and speech-language pathology)
4 years
10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and a third subject at 50 percent (45 percent for SC, ST and PwD candidates), by entrance exam.
Clinical work with hearing tests and therapy. We found no rule that bars or allows deaf applicants, so ask the institute how it supports them.

blocks.heading: Routes That Filter You Twice
rows: Government jobs
A written-exam rank high enough to land within the vacancies reserved for deaf and hard of hearing.
Medical and document verification, and a check that the post has been identified for your category.
Special education and ISL teaching
Admission to an RCI-recognised course through an entrance exam or merit list, with limited seats.
RCI registration and a school or institute willing to hire. Posts are few and often fixed-pay.
Audiology and speech-language pathology
A national or institute entrance exam for a small number of seats.
Supervised practice and building patient trust before a private clinic pays.

blocks.heading: Career Options for Deaf
rows: Software and data
Hiring managers; later, clients buying a finished project.
Live project, repository, referral.
State in one line what problem you solve and for whom.
Digital marketing and e-commerce
Brands and online sellers; your own shoppers.
Order and lead numbers, referrals.
Log leads and orders in one sheet and follow up once, in writing.
Design, video, photography
Studios, agencies, direct clients.
Portfolio pieces and referrals.
Turn one deliverable into a fixed-price package.
Own business and trades
Local customers.
Repeat orders and a listing you control.
Send a written quote stating scope and payment terms before starting.
ISL teaching and deaf education
Schools for deaf children, institutes, NGOs, families.
An RCI-recognised qualification and parents' word of mouth.
Offer one trial lesson, then a clear monthly fee.
Government jobs
The government as employer. Sales skills matter mostly for a side income or the next move.
Rank, not marketing.
Build a second skill that produces visible work.

visuals.heading: Speech-To-Text and AI

items.text: Live captions on video calls and in phone apps make everyday meetings far easier to follow.
Speech-to-text gives you a written record to check afterwards.
AI assistants can summarise a meeting recording, draft an email and explain a long document.
Chat and shared documents move quick questions off the phone.
